statement.p: The velocity \displaystyle{v} of a falling object varies directly with the time \displaystyle{t} of the fall. If after 4.00 seconds, the velocity of an object is 128 feet per second, what is the velocity after 6.00 seconds?

solution.p: Varying directly means \displaystyle{v}={k}\cdot{t}. We know \displaystyle{128}={k}{4.00}, so \displaystyle{k}=\frac{{128}}{{4.00}}={32}.
Thus after 6.00 seconds we would have \displaystyle{v}={32}\cdot{6.00}={192}\approx{192}.
